note: Rejected pairs from batch 9, the final investigation batch. All four medicines were rejected 4/4 and no URL is proposed for any of them. 60 and 90 are product ranges rather than SKUs; 67 and 82 are dosage-form ambiguities. Nothing was accepted to raise coverage on the last batch. No medicine record was changed.

verifier.evidence: No unqualified 'Band-Aid' product page exists; only the Flexi / Washproof / Waterproof / Square named variants at multiple counts are listed.
verifier.notes: PRODUCT RANGE, NOT A SKU. No pharmacy offers an unqualified 'Band-Aid' product page. The brand is sold only as named constructions -- Flexi, Washproof, Waterproof, Square Regular, and the Flexi Antiseptic Spots/Patches/Strips -- which differ in backing material, water resistance and shape, and each exists at several counts (1, 10, 20, 30, 100, 100+30). Pack count is identity-bearing for a dressing, the same reason medicines 30 and 45 are deprioritised. The only unqualified 'Band-Aid' destinations found were 1mg's brand CATEGORY page and Apollo's brand listing page, which are not product pages. Secondary observation, not acted on: 1mg names the marketer 'JNTL Consumer Health (India) Pvt. Ltd.' -- the post-Kenvue-separation entity for J&J consumer brands -- while our record says 'Johnson & Johnson'. Even had a single SKU existed, that would have needed checking first.

verifier.evidence: Pudin Hara Pearls, Active Liquid, Antacid Suspension and the Fizz sachets are all listed; our record names no dosage form and no composition.
verifier.notes: DOSAGE-FORM AMBIGUITY. Neither our name 'Pudin Hara' nor our description fixes a dosage form, and the brand ships at least five presentations with materially different compositions: Pearls (soft gelatin capsules, pudina satva + hingul), Active Liquid (10ml / 30ml concentrate), Antacid Suspension / Syrup (170ml / 200ml), and Lemon Fizz / Fanto Fizz effervescent sachets. This is the same rule applied to Febrex Plus (62) and Digene (22). It is deliberately NOT the Zincovit (36) or Sinarest (63) case: those records carry a description that names the dosage form ('...tablet...'), which is what allowed the base SKU to be chosen there. Ours names none. Recommended for DEPRIORITIZED_IDS.

verifier.evidence: Liv.52 tablet, DS tablet, syrup, drops and HB capsule are all listed; our record names no dosage form.
verifier.notes: DOSAGE-FORM AMBIGUITY. Liv.52 ships as tablet (100s), DS tablet (60s, double strength), syrup (100ml / 200ml), drops (60ml / 100ml / 120ml) and the HB capsule, plus a Forte Vet line. Our record is plain 'Liv 52' and our description -- 'Herbal formulation that supports liver function and digestion' -- names no dosage form, so the base SKU cannot be selected without guessing. Same rule as medicine 67 above and as Febrex Plus (62). The tablet is the best-known presentation, but 'best known' is precisely the inference the zero-false-accept standard forbids. Manufacturer was not the blocker: 1mg states both 'The Himalaya Drug Company' and 'Himalaya Wellness Company', consistent with our record and with the entity-granularity note already recorded for Evecare (medicine 55). Recommended for DEPRIORITIZED_IDS: this one becomes eligible immediately once a dosage_form column exists.

verifier.evidence: No unqualified 'Hansaplast' product page exists; only the named wound-dressing, heat, belladonna and corn plaster lines at multiple counts.
verifier.notes: PRODUCT RANGE, NOT A SKU. No unqualified 'Hansaplast' product page exists. The range spans three different therapeutic categories: wound dressings (Washproof, Regular, Spot, Jumbo, Antiseptic bandages), pain-relief plasters (Lion Heat Plaster with capsicum, Lion Belladonna Plaster) and a keratolytic (Corn Plaster, salicylic acid), plus first-aid kits and crepe bandages. Our description 'adhesive plasters and bandages for minor wound protection' does narrow this to the dressing category, but within it the Washproof / Regular / Spot / Jumbo constructions still differ and each is sold at several counts (8, 10, 20, 50, 100, 100+36, 250). Pack count is identity-bearing for a dressing. Same outcome and same reasoning as Band-Aid (60) in this batch.
